record.original_question: What is the bit complexity of solving an $n x n$ linear system with $nnz(A)$ non-zeros? In particular, does the $~ O(n* nnz(A))$ runtime extend to the Word-RAM model.

evidence.quote: What is the bit complexity of solving an $n\times n$ linear system with $\text{nnz}(A)$ non-zeros? In particular, does the $\tilde O(n\cdot \text{nnz}(A))$ runtime extend to the Word-RAM model.

artifact.self_contained_problem: Consider the problem of solving a linear system $Ax=b$ where $A\in\mathbb{Q}^{n\times n}$ is given as input together with $b\in\mathbb{Q}^n$, and let $\mathrm{nnz}(A)$ denote the number of nonzero entries of $A$. The goal is to output, in the Word-RAM model of computation (with words of size $O(\log n)$ bits and unit-cost operations on such words), a vector $\tilde x\in\mathbb{Q}^n$ approximating a solution to within $1/\mathrm{poly}(n)$ accuracy, while accounting for the bit length of all intermediate quantities. Determine the bit complexity, as a function of $n$ and $\mathrm{nnz}(A)$ (and the condition number $\kappa(A)$), of solving such an $n\times n$ linear system. In particular, does there exist a Word-RAM algorithm that achieves running time $\widetilde O(n\cdot \mathrm{nnz}(A))$ (up to polylogarithmic factors in $n$ and $\kappa(A)$) for solving sparse linear systems, matching the bound known in the real-arithmetic / exact-arithmetic model?
artifact.category_tag: bit complexity of sparse linear system solvers
artifact.status_search_result: The question of whether the $\widetilde O(n\cdot\mathrm{nnz}(A))$ runtime for sparse linear system solving extends to the Word-RAM model has seen recent progress. Peng–Vempala (2020) gave an algorithm faster than matrix multiplication for sparse systems, and follow-up work (e.g., "The Bit Complexity of Efficient Continuous Optimization", 2023, and "Numerical Linear Algebra in Linear Space", 2025) has tightened bit-complexity bounds in the Word-RAM model. However, an exact $\widetilde O(n\cdot\mathrm{nnz}(A))$ Word-RAM bound matching the real-RAM analysis has not been established in full generality, so the question appears to remain partially open.

status_evidence.title: Solving Sparse Linear Systems Faster than Matrix Multiplication
status_evidence.snippet: Algorithm solves sparse linear systems asymptotically faster than matrix multiplication; bit complexity O(n^2.331645) for poly-conditioned matrices with Õ(n) nonzeros.
status_evidence.claim: Subsequent work gave a sparse solver beating matrix multiplication, with explicit bit-complexity bounds, but did not establish Õ(n·nnz(A)) in Word-RAM.

status_evidence.title: The Bit Complexity of Efficient Continuous Optimization
status_evidence.snippet: Studies bit complexity of continuous optimization including linear systems in the Word-RAM model.
status_evidence.claim: Recent work analyzes bit complexity of linear-system-style solvers in the Word-RAM model.

status_evidence.title: Numerical Linear Algebra in Linear Space
status_evidence.snippet: Improves space and bit complexity of numerical linear algebra primitives.
status_evidence.claim: Ongoing progress on bit-complexity bounds for sparse linear algebra.
